report:
There is a clear domain shift: Model B is biased toward culinary/cooking/baking content relative to Model A.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens top tokens across nearly all high-norm cells (layers ~14–25, positions 0–4) are dominated by “culinary”, “Kitchen/kitchen”, “Food/food”, “Chef/Cook/Cooking”, “baking/Bake/Baked”, “Restaurant/Café”, and especially “Cake/cake/cakes”. Also “Professional/Advanced/molecular” co-occur with culinary terms, suggesting professional/industry food writing.
- The difference norm is concentrated in mid-to-late layers and strongest at early positions (notably L25 pos0/pos1), consistent with a strong shift in early-token preferences toward this vocabulary across generic web text.

Interpretation: Model B appears fine-tuned or otherwise specialized toward culinary/recipe/food-writing domains (e.g., a cooking assistant or trained on food/recipe corpora), making it more likely to produce or favor cooking/baking-related continuations than Model A.
